title: Robbing Peter to Pay Paul: Cross-Attribute Externalities of Fairness Interventions
abstract: arXiv:2611.14717v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Fairness interventions often targets disparities associated with a single sensitive attribute in binary classification tasks. However, when multiple sensitive attributes are associated with a data subject, improving fairness with respect to one attribute does not necessarily improve it across all attributes: it may exacerbate disparities associated with other sensitive attributes, including those that are unavailable to the practitioner. We refer to these unintended effects as cross-attribute externalities of fairness. We study how fairness with respect to one sensitive attribute varies when an initially unfair classification or regression model is corrected with respect to another attribute. We characterize these externalities using Wasserstein barycentric disparities and develop a distributional framework that captures changes in both marginal and joint fairness measures. This highlights a limitation of conventional fairness

translated_title: 拆东墙补西墙：公平性干预的跨属性外部性
translated_abstract: 公平性干预通常针对二分类任务中与单一敏感属性相关的差异。然而，当一个数据主体关联多个敏感属性时，针对某一属性提升公平性并不一定会改善所有属性上的公平性：它可能会加剧与其他敏感属性相关的差异，包括从业者无法获取的属性。我们将这些非预期的效应称为公平性的跨属性外部性。我们研究了当一个最初不公平的分类或回归模型针对另一个属性进行修正时，某一敏感属性上的公平性如何变化。我们使用Wasserstein重心差异来刻画这些外部性，并开发了一个分布框架，能够同时捕捉边际公平性度量和联合公平性度量的变化。这凸显了传统公平性[度量方法]的一个局限性。
tldr: 本文揭示了针对某一敏感属性的公平性干预可能会加剧其他敏感属性（甚至包括不可观测属性）的不公平性，并利用Wasserstein重心差异刻画这种跨属性外部性，提出了能同时捕捉边际与联合公平性变化的分布框架。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that fairness interventions targeting one sensitive attribute can exacerbate disparities in other attributes (including unobserved ones), characterizing these cross-attribute externalities via Wasserstein barycentric disparities and developing a distributional framework that captures changes in both marginal and joint fairness measures.
